findings.reason: the section's premise and status are stale against its own recorded arms, so a dispatched node re-diagnoses already-repaired tests instead of closing the section, and the followup that recommends building §1 first steers the whole plan at it.
findings.text: §1 asserts "Thirteen tests in tests/standard_names fail at every base and head measured on 2026-11-11", but the two §1 comments record otherwise: the gap-rules arm measured base `12 failed / 8639 passed` and head `1 failed / 8654 passed`, and the other arm records that four of the remaining ids (catalog-layout ordering-cycle and the three manifest-generability ids) "were already green at base and needed no change", that the cascade-calibration id "does not fail, it skips", and that the one real failure (NC-25) closed at head `276 passed, 2 skipped, EXIT=0`. The section is therefore complete in fact while still declared `implementable`, and its summary meta line still reads "Fix or own the 13 tests red on main". A node dispatched on §1 as written mounts a compute-partition suite run to hunt thirteen failures of which the plan's own evidence shows at most seven ever failed and none fail now

findings.reason: a worker greps a test id that does not exist and cannot tell whether the test was renamed, deleted, or never had that name, which is a blocker-shaped detour on the first of the plan's sections.
findings.text: §1 lists `test_geometry_enumeration_collapse.py::test_unregistered_arc_endpoint_rejects_the_ordinal_compound`, which resolves to no test: the file defines `test_unregistered_locus_rejects_the_ordinal_compound` (`tests/standard_names/test_geometry_enumeration_collapse.py:226`), and the plan's own closure comment names that locus id as one of the seven ids that pass. The `arc_endpoint` spelling appears nowhere in the tree

findings.reason: without a stated endpoint for the fixture-absence skip, the node would close §1 having verified eleven of thirteen ids and leave the twelfth unmeasured, which is precisely the regeneration state §1 exists to remove.
findings.text: §1's measure is "the default tests/standard_names run on a compute partition reports none of the 13 ids failing at the merged head", which is satisfied by non-execution: the cascade-calibration id skips because its two frozen receipt files are absent from the reckon store, so its greenness in the gate comes from the `skipif`, not from the behaviour the test was written to assert. The same done-when forbids an id being "skipped or deleted" but offers no endpoint for a skip that comes from a missing fixture rather than from the node's own choice, so the section can close green over a guard that no longer runs

findings.reason: the section is deferred and its rows are explicitly re-homed as sections of their own once the first upstream catalog release is cut, so no node dispatches against this text and the gap costs nothing until that release lands.
findings.text: §7 carries eight hours of repair rows and an explicit re-confirmation rule, but no "Done when" line and no negative control, so the section has no checkable endpoint of its own and its status can only move by the prose sentence that each row becomes a section
